problem: Learnable ObjectNav policies are robust to sensor noise but suffer from a sim-to-real gap, while classical non-learnable modular methods are accurate but brittle to noise. Neither alone works well in both simulation and on real robots.
motivation: Agents in human-centric environments must explore unseen areas and reach objects humans care about. Combining the accuracy of classical modules with the robustness of learned modules, and training the learned ones to be less environment-dependent, could give reliable real-world ObjectNav.
key_idea: A hybrid ObjectNav framework, SkillFusion, that switches between non-learnable (accurate) and learnable (noise-robust) skill modules, with the learnable parts trained to be less environment-dependent to reduce the sim-to-real gap.
insight: The abstract states that non-learnable modules are more accurate while learnable ones are more robust to sensor noise, so a switcher between them combines both strengths. Training the learnable modules to be less environment-dependent is meant to mitigate the sim-to-real gap. No ablations are available because only the abstract was provided.
method: Non-learnable modules: classical, more accurate navigation/exploration skills.
Learnable modules: trained policies that are more robust to sensor noise.
SkillFusion switcher: selects between the non-learnable and learnable skills during navigation.
Environment-independent training: learnable modules are trained to depend less on the environment, to reduce the sim-to-real gap.

setting.backbone: hybrid: classical modules plus learned policy modules (details not given in abstract)
